title: Break the odds-fitting circularity
summary: The Harville baseline fits latent strengths TO market odds, so it can only reproduce the market, never beat it. The research model must instead predict from features (with odds as ONE feature) and be …
text: break the odds-fitting circularity modelling circularity edge the harville baseline fits latent strengths to market odds, so it can only reproduce the market, never beat it. the research model must instead predict from features (with odds as one feature) and be scored against realized results + clv. edge = divergence from the market's implied distribution x superior calibration. this reframes what the model layer is for.

title: CLV is the north-star leading indicator
summary: In an efficient pari-mutuel market, beating the CLOSING line is the strongest available signal of true edge, and it exists for every race whether or not we bet — partially rescuing the ~800-races/year…
text: clv is the north-star leading indicator clv evaluation odds-ticks in an efficient pari-mutuel market, beating the closing line is the strongest available signal of true edge, and it exists for every race whether or not we bet — partially rescuing the ~800-races/year sparse-feedback problem. built the odds tick store (hkjc.data.odds_ticks) + hkjc.eval.clv to make it measurable. negative open->close drift = informed money (steam).

text: pool takeout is not uniform — 0.175 is win/pla/qin/qpl only takeout betting-rules ev takeout ranges ~17.5% (win/place/quinella/qpl) up to ~25% (quartet/first 4); trio/forecast ~19.5%, tierce ~22%. a 5% modelled edge is profitable at 17.5% and underwater at 25%. always net edge against the specific pool's takeout. harville_model's takeout_rate=0.175 default must be overridden per pool. rates are season-tunable — prefer scraping live estimateddividend/jpests.

title: Jackpot carryover windows can be structurally +EV
summary: Double Trio, Triple Trio and Six Up carry an un-won jackpot forward (~7.5% jackpot reserve + 0.5% operator skim). On a carryover meeting the pool can pay out more than is bet that day => effective tak…
text: jackpot carryover windows can be structurally +ev jackpot triple-trio six-up +ev double trio, triple trio and six up carry an un-won jackpot forward (~7.5% jackpot reserve + 0.5% operator skim). on a carryover meeting the pool can pay out more than is bet that day => effective takeout on new money goes negative, independent of any modelling skill. worth a dedicated mechanical detector; size the buy as a flexi-unit combinatorial cover, not a single bet.

title: Evaluation harness is the objective function — build it before optimizing
summary: Step 2 built hkjc.eval into the loop's objective function: calibration (log-loss/Brier/ECE/RPS + multiclass race_win_log_loss), walk-forward folds with an embargo measured in MEETING-DAYS (not calenda…
text: evaluation harness is the objective function — build it before optimizing evaluation harness walk-forward lockbox fdr step 2 built hkjc.eval into the loop's objective function: calibration (log-loss/brier/ece/rps + multiclass race_win_log_loss), walk-forward folds with an embargo measured in meeting-days (not calendar days), a sealed lockbox that enforces read-once via a persisted access log, and multiple-testing control (benjamini-hochberg fdr + deflated/probabilistic sharpe). the harness owns splitting+scoring; the model supplies fit_predict(train,test)->preds. that boundary keeps the judge un-gameable from inside the model.

title: Deflated Sharpe needs an HONEST trial count
summary: DSR / expected-max-Sharpe haircuts a result by how many strategies were tried (best-of-N is guaranteed to look good on ~800 races/yr). The math is only as honest as n_trials. The orchestrator MUST tra…
text: deflated sharpe needs an honest trial count selection overfitting fdr trial-count dsr / expected-max-sharpe haircuts a result by how many strategies were tried (best-of-n is guaranteed to look good on ~800 races/yr). the math is only as honest as n_trials. the orchestrator must track the true number of hypotheses tested (candidate the ledger as the source of truth) and feed it in — otherwise selection silently under-corrects and we bank noise. random splits are banned for the same reason: horses/jockeys/trainers/going persist across meetings.

title: Results-trained conditional-logit model breaks the circularity (works)
summary: Step 4 shipped hkjc.model.ConditionalLogit: McFadden conditional logit, strength s_i=beta.x_i, within-race win prob = softmax; fit by MLE of actual winners (convex NLL, L-BFGS-B with analytic gradient…
text: results-trained conditional-logit model breaks the circularity (works) model conditional-logit circularity win-prediction step 4 shipped hkjc.model.conditionallogit: mcfadden conditional logit, strength s_i=beta.x_i, within-race win prob = softmax; fit by mle of actual winners (convex nll, l-bfgs-b with analytic gradient x^t(p-y); no intercept since a race-constant cancels in softmax; features standardized + mean-imputed; l2 ridge). market-implied prob is just one feature, so the model can diverge from and beat the market rather than reproduce it. conditional_logit_fit_predict plugs straight into the step-2 harness; strengths() feed plackettlucemodel for place/quinella sim. validated: trained on winners only (no odds), beats uniform by ~37% on multiclass race_win_log_loss out-of-sample across 4 walk-forward folds. note: binary one-vs-rest log-loss can favour flat uniform out-of-sample (loser rows punish confident winners) — judge win models on the multiclass race_win_log_loss, the proper score. model layer is now a package (base/plackett_luce/conditional_logit/baselines).

text: first real backtest: crude model does not beat the hkjc win market (efficient) backtest market-efficiency win negative-result benter built a real w/p/q dataset from result pages: 3216 runner-rows, 261 races, 26 meetings (2026-03-01..05-31). walk-forward (5 folds) race_win_log_loss: uniform 2.506; market baseline 2.070; clogit[log_market] 2.077 (-0.3% vs market); clogit[+draw,wt] 2.090 (-1.0%); clogit[+draw,wt,declwt] 2.099 (-1.4%). flat-stake roi proxy (payout at closing odds) negative at every edge threshold (-0.187 @ edge>0, -0.043 @ edge>10% on 60 bets). conclusion: with crude features (draw + weight + the market sp) on a small sample, no edge over the closing market — the win market is highly efficient and the harness correctly refuses to manufacture a fake edge (this validates the objective function). clogit[log_market] ~= market confirms no info loss (coef~1; favourite-longshot correction negligible here); extra crude features overfit tiny first folds and hurt. path forward: edge needs richer features (official rating, recent form, speed/pace, speedpro, the chinese alt-data + video axes) and more data (full seasons), not this feature set. result page has no rating; must join the racecard/graphql or speedpro for fundamentals.

title: Quant team verdict: build the Jackpot Carryover Harvester; model-edge exotics are look-ahead traps
summary: A 6-analyst + adversarial-verify + synthesis workflow ranked HKJC arb/exotic strategies. WINNER: Jackpot Carryover Harvester (Triple Trio/Double Trio/Six Up) as a DETECTOR + research instrument (not a…
text: quant team verdict: build the jackpot carryover harvester; model-edge exotics are look-ahead traps strategy jackpot-carryover exotics look-ahead workflow a 6-analyst + adversarial-verify + synthesis workflow ranked hkjc arb/exotic strategies. winner: jackpot carryover harvester (triple trio/double trio/six up) as a detector + research instrument (not a deployment). it is the only proposal with a structural edge (un-won jackpot carries ~85% net forward, so new money on a carryover meeting faces negative effective takeout on the aggregate pool: eff_takeout = (1-net) - c/g; flag when c/g > 1-net ~ 0.15) and the only one backtestable on data we can assemble now (live jpests/estimateddividend/poolinvs already in live.py; realized settlement already in get_race_dividends which maps dt/tt/6up). key warning the team surfaced: every model-edge exotic play (qin/qpl coherence, place arb, steam) is not backtestable on our data — result pages publish only the winning combo's dividend, never the pre-close crowd matrix of losing combos you must price to detect an overlay; and selecting bets on the realized settlement dividend (as bets.price_dividends edge does) is look-ahead the walk-forward embargo forbids. the tau place-bias play (proposal 6) is empirically falsified (optimum at tau=1.0). carryover weaknesses to respect: endogenous dilution (settle at final crowd; publicized carryover invites other harvesters), partial flexi cover still leans on a barely-calibrated win-odds harville top_set(3), and lottery variance means it may be +ev yet statistically dark (few events/season). build plan: jackpot ledger from dividend remarks -> reconstruct c,g -> detector (ev two ways: naive vs estimateddividend + stressed late pool) -> flexi cover via simulator+pareto -> score through walkforward/fdr/lockbox -> forward capture. model-edge exotic lines need a forward live odds-tick capture season first.

text: gate 1 passed: carryover windows are frequent and large enough (target the modest ones) jackpot-carryover gate-1 frequency chase-money backfill backfill research (racing news + scmp). triple trio (3 trios) and six-up six win bonus roll over frequently (the hard pools go unwon more often than won; double trio is usually won/small). fresh tt net pools collapsed ~hk$10m->~hk$2m while carried jackpots routinely sit hk$3-30m (rare hk$60-100m, capped at hk$100m since 1997). so c/g on carryover meetings is regularly >> 0.15, often >=1 -> structurally +ev windows exist, plausibly dozens/season. key refinement: chase money floods publicized big jackpots and erodes the edge, so the cleaner edge is likely in modest, under-publicized carryovers (small hk$2-5m tt rolls), not the headline hk$60m ones. gate-2 constraints: 17-19% takeout, the hk$100m cap, chase dilution, combinatorial cover cost. backfill sources: racing news pre-meeting announcements (racingnews.hkjc.com/english/yyyy/mm/dd/slug; enumerate via date archives/feed/sitemap) for c; localresults by racedate for won/carried outcome. data points e.g. 26nov2025 hv tt c~2.5m est~5m; 20sep2023 hv tt c>17.7m est~26m; 6jun2021 st tt c>61m pool 106m paid 23m/unit.

text: rating + form do not beat the win market (efficient w.r.t. fundamentals) model market-efficiency rating form negative-result richer-features experiment (140 races, 14 meetings, 2026-04-15..05-31, horse-form-derived rating + trailing form). walk-forward race_win_log_loss: market 2.048 baseline; clogit[market] 2.049 (-0.0%, reproduces market, coef~1, no info loss); clogit[market,rating] 2.064 (-0.8%); clogit[market,rating,form] 2.167 (-5.8%). conclusion: official rating and recent form add nothing over the closing win line and overfit on small data -> the market already prices standard fundamentals efficiently. strengthens journal 0011: a win model edge will not come from standard fundamentals; it needs information the market lacks (trip comments/corunning, sectionals/trajectory, alt-data). reinforces the two right lines: carryover structural edge (main) + dense-data/trajectory (information) for any model edge. caveats: 140 races underpowered; generate_historical_data truncates history so trailing-form features are noisy (part of why form hurt most) -- a cleaner full-history form build might do less badly but is unlikely to beat market given the rating result.

title: TT cover backtest: naive top-5 box is unprofitable & hit-rate-bound (and dark)
summary: experiments/backtest_carryover_cover.py over 2026-03..05: 18 won Triple Trios (14 settleable). A fixed top-5 box cover (1000 combos/event, win-odds leg models, settled at REAL dividends, dilution igno…
text: tt cover backtest: naive top-5 box is unprofitable & hit-rate-bound (and dark) jackpot-carryover backtest cover hit-rate statistically-dark experiments/backtest_carryover_cover.py over 2026-03..05: 18 won triple trios (14 settleable). a fixed top-5 box cover (1000 combos/event, win-odds leg models, settled at real dividends, dilution ignored=optimistic): hit rate 7% (1/14), total pnl -1,064 on 14,000 staked, roi -7.6%. the one hit was a low dividend (12,936); the big carryovers (e.g. 810,610 on 03/11) were missed. read: (1) the cover hit-rate is the binding constraint -- top-5 rarely contains the exact trio in all 3 legs; (2) this bet all tt events, not just +ev carryover windows (we can't identify those historically without c), so it's not the real strategy; (3) 14 events is statistically dark (one hit dominates) -- exactly the quant-team warning. implication: the carryover structural edge is real in aggregate but capturing it needs (a) filtering to high-c/g windows [needs live c from the flywheel], (b) cover-size optimization + a better leg model, (c) far more events. historical backtest can't validate the strategy; forward live capture (modal) is the critical path.

text: sectional physics features do not beat the market (3rd consecutive negative) trajectory sectional physics market-efficiency negative-result trajectory-line kill/confirm (269 races, 27 meetings, 2026-03..05). trailing (prior-run) field-relative sectional energetics — finishing speed, early speed, fade=last/best section. walk-forward race_win_log_loss: market 2.054 baseline; clogit[mkt] 2.064 (-0.5%); clogit[mkt,finish,fade] 2.108 (-2.6%); clogit[mkt,all-sectional] 2.115 (-3.0%). sectional pace/fade features hurt, same as rating/form. third consecutive negative (journal 0011 crude, 0023 rating/form, now sectionals): the win market is efficient w.r.t. odds/draw/weight/rating/form/sectional-pace. key insight for next step: sectionals capture pace & fade (which the market prices via the chart) but not ground-lost (actual meters travelled / wide trips) -- that signal is invisible to section times and only recoverable from the 2d video trajectory. so ground-lost via video is the one plausibly-unpriced signal left. caveats: small sample, trailing features noisy (few prior runs/horse in a 3-month window), crude features (field-relative section times, not a full cp-w' fit with real distances) -- but the consistent 3x direction makes more sectional engineering low-value. decision per plan: if sectionals yield nothing, move to video for finer granularity (ground-lost).

title: Trip-trouble gate NEGATIVE -> video NOT justified; close the model-edge line
summary: Gate experiment (144 races, 16 meetings; 179 troubled-last-start rows). Prior-run trouble from stewards' running comments (blocked/no-clear-run/checked, ~12% rate). Walk-forward race_win_log_loss: mar…
text: trip-trouble gate negative -> video not justified; close the model-edge line trouble video-gate market-efficiency model-edge-closed strategy gate experiment (144 races, 16 meetings; 179 troubled-last-start rows). prior-run trouble from stewards' running comments (blocked/no-clear-run/checked, ~12% rate). walk-forward race_win_log_loss: market 2.069 baseline; clogit[mkt] 2.078 (-0.4%); clogit[mkt,trouble_last] 2.154 (-4.1%); +rate 2.154 (-4.1%). trouble hurts. likely cause: the 'unlucky last time' angle is the most famous handicapping angle -> crowd already (over)bets it, so troubled horses are if anything over-rated, not under. gate verdict: the stewards' trouble notes are a stronger signal than a first cv pass would extract; they don't beat the market, so video re-deriving the lateral/ground-lost signal won't either -> do not build the video cv pipeline (saved weeks). fourth consecutive negative (0011 crude, 0023 rating/form, 0025 sectional-physics, now trouble): the hk win market is efficient w.r.t. every extractable signal. strategic conclusion: close the model-edge hunt; the carryover structural edge is the only viable line and is compounding live data via the modal flywheel. caveat: samples small (3-month windows) but the 4x consistency + efficient-market prior make this the right resource call. revisit only with full-season data or a fundamentally new data source the market truly cannot see.

text: video feasibility probe: aerial = tracking-data render; cv-extractable but low-ev video aerial tracking-data feasibility cv probed the aerial replay. findings: (1) directly downloadable mp4, deterministic url streaminghkjc-a.akamaihd.net/hdflash/replay-aerial/{yyyy}/{yyyymmdd}/{nn}/eng/replay-aerial_{yyyymmdd}_{nn}_eng_{1200|2500}kbps.mp4 (1080p/25fps). (2) the 'aerial' is a split screen: real broadcast (left) + 'aerial virtual view' (right) = a synthetic top-down reconstruction rendered from hkjc's horse position tracking (gps/rfid; disclaimer warns mobile-phone interference may reduce accuracy). (3) so the 2d positions we want (lateral, ground-lost) exist and are visible as per-horse silk sprites -- but only as a rendered video; getvideoinfo api exposes no raw position feed (videofound/videodronefound metadata only; a real 'drone' video may also exist). (4) cv extraction feasible but not trivial: naive saturation-blob on the synthetic panel gave 97 false blobs (textured track); needs silk-template matching + temporal tracking + homography -- a real days/weeks build. key: the stewards' running comments we already tested (gate, journal 0026) are the expert interpretation of this same tracking data + all angles, and they don't beat the market -> cv re-deriving the positions (less expertly, from a disclaimed-accuracy render) is very unlikely to. the one genuinely-new signal is quantitative ground-lost (meters) for the energetics model, which stewards don't encode numerically -- but cost+accuracy+4x-efficiency-prior make ev low. verdict: feasible, not worth the full build; revisit only if a raw position-data feed is found or the energetics model shows promise and needs ground-lost.

title: First-principles energetics model also fails to beat the market (5th negative)
summary: Generative critical-velocity model (269 races, 27 meetings). Trailing pace-neutral (v_c, W') -> EnergeticsRaceModel simulates finishing times -> win probs. Walk-forward race_win_log_loss: market 2.049…
text: first-principles energetics model also fails to beat the market (5th negative) energetics first-principles market-efficiency model-edge-closed generative critical-velocity model (269 races, 27 meetings). trailing pace-neutral (v_c, w') -> energeticsracemodel simulates finishing times -> win probs. walk-forward race_win_log_loss: market 2.049 baseline; physics-only 2.610 (-27%, worse than uniform -> raw physics poorly calibrated); clogit[mkt] 2.061 (-0.6%); clogit[mkt,physics] 2.066 (-0.8%, physics adds nothing, marginally hurts). the mechanistic model carries no independent signal beyond the closing line. fifth consecutive negative across both paradigms: statistical (crude 0011, rating/form 0023, sectional 0025, trouble 0026) and first-principles dynamical (energetics, this). conclusion: the hk win market is efficient w.r.t. everything we can extract -- unsurprising, as it's one of the most heavily-modelled markets in the world (benter et al. already run exactly these speed/stamina/pace models with decades of data). model-edge line is closed. caveats: 3-month samples; trailing (v_c,w') noisy (1-2 prior runs/horse); time_noise uncalibrated -- but the combined logit optimally reweights the physics feature and still fails, and the 5x consistency + strong prior make this robust for resource allocation. only remaining model-edge lever is full-season data (low prior, big cost) -- not recommended over the carryover structural line, which is the project's real edge and is compounding live data.

title: Tier-A traffic model: focus Happy Valley; track geometry + movable rail captured
summary: User directive: build the Tier-A interacting/traffic-flow race model for ONE racecourse, using real HKJC track specs, and account for the MOVABLE RAIL (the rail shifts out meeting-to-meeting, changing…
text: tier-a traffic model: focus happy valley; track geometry + movable rail captured traffic-model tier-a happy-valley track-geometry movable-rail draw-bias user directive: build the tier-a interacting/traffic-flow race model for one racecourse, using real hkjc track specs, and account for the movable rail (the rail shifts out meeting-to-meeting, changing geometry/draw-bias per race -- captured via the per-race `course` field). chosen venue: happy valley (strongest draw bias in hk, simplest single 1450m bend-dominated circuit). specs captured in hkjc.model.track.happy_valley (official figures): circumference 1450m, right-handed/clockwise, course->width a 30.5m ... c+3 19.5m (rail out -> ~11m narrower), home straight ~300-338m. bend map from sampling points: home straight [0,300], bends [300,770] (sanatorium/crescent/the rock), back straight [770,920], bends [920,1450] (hkfc/stable+top) -> bend_fraction(1200)~0.63, so draw exposure is persistent. the draw-bias mechanism: on a turn, inner lane = shorter arc; low draw holding the rail runs less ground (off-rail metres x turn angle = ground lost). sha tin specs also recorded (430m straight, less bias) for later. next: build the cellular-automaton/car-following racemodel using this geometry + the (v_c,w') energetics engine; draw->initial lane; blocked if horse ahead + no lateral gap. tier-b (true lateral lanes) needs aerial-video trajectories.

title: Tier-A traffic model built; geometric draw bias EMERGES (needs calibration)
summary: hkjc.model.traffic.TrafficRaceModel: vectorized agent-based sim. Each horse runs its energetic even-pace target v_c*(1+W'/D) (reduces to the energetics model with empty track) but is subject to traffi…
text: tier-a traffic model built; geometric draw bias emerges (needs calibration) traffic-model tier-a draw-bias emergent needs-calibration hkjc.model.traffic.trafficracemodel: vectorized agent-based sim. each horse runs its energetic even-pace target v_c*(1+w'/d) (reduces to the energetics model with empty track) but is subject to traffic: car-following (capped behind a same-lane horse within follow_gap), lane-change/gap-acceptance when blocked (stochastic, moving out), drift back to rail when clear, and bend ground-loss (ground_factor = 1 + off*curvature on turns; draw -> starting lateral offset, width from the day's course). uses hkjc.model.track hv geometry. validation (key): with equal-ability horses, the inner-draw advantage emerges purely from geometry -- hv 1200m a course: draw1 win 32% monotonically down to draw12 0.6%. mechanism works (draw bias produced, not fitted); ability can also overcome a wide draw (tested). but currently over-amplified vs reality -> needs calibration of (bend_curvature, speed noise, lane params) to the empirical hv draw-bias curve (hkjc drawstatistics or our results), then the edge test vs market (esp. unusual draw/pace configs). tier-b (true lateral lanes) still needs aerial-video trajectories. ~17s/8k-sample sim (per-step o(n^2) vectorized over samples).

title: Consolidated geometry + canonical Race domain object for agent-based modelling
summary: Consolidated the codebase around the agent-based-modelling approach and integrated race-course geometry as first-class reference data. **Geometry (hkjc.track, promoted out of hkjc.model.track).** Now …
text:
consolidated geometry + canonical race domain object for agent-based modelling geometry traffic-model refactor sha-tin happy-valley abm consolidated the codebase around the agent-based-modelling approach and integrated race-course geometry as first-class reference data.

**geometry (hkjc.track, promoted out of hkjc.model.track).** now covers all hk regimes, not just happy valley:
- happy_valley: turf 1450m, bend-dominated (bend map from sectional sampling points).
- sha_tin_turf: 1900m galloping oval, 430m home straight, long straights => weaker draw bias.
- sha_tin_straight: the separate 1000m sprint chute with no bends => no bend-geometry draw bias (only watering gradient, not modelled). track_for("st",1000) returns this, not the oval.
- sha_tin_awt: dirt 1560m, fixed single rail, uniform 22.8m.
resolver track_for(venue, distance, surface) picks the right geometry. per-course widths/home-straights are official hkjc figures; st oval/awt bend *boundaries* are two-turn reconstructions from circumference+home-straight (approximate, documented).

**canonical race/runner domain object (hkjc.race).** bundles runners + geometry + conditions; resolves .geometry/.width/.bend_fraction and builds any model in one call (.traffic_model(), .energetics_model(), .plackett_luce()). constructors from_results(df) / from_racecard(df) / from_runners(). surface inferred from the all weather track label (going codes alone are ambiguous: both turf and awt have good). this is the abm seam — no more passing loose parallel arrays.

**validation.** geometry now produces the correct venue ordering purely from physics: at 1200m, hv (62% on turns) yields a 29x inner/outer win ratio vs sha tin turf (42% on turns) at only 3.1x — hv draw bias >> st, as in reality. still over-amplified in absolute terms (calibration pending), but the relative structure is right and emergent.

**cleanup.** removed the four falsified-model experiment scripts (form/market/sectional/trouble). kept energetics (basis of the traffic model) + the live carryover/capture runners. 103 tests pass (was 91), ruff clean. version 1.6.0.

next: calibrate bend_curvature/noise to the empirical per-venue draw curves (drawstatistics / results), then test the calibrated interacting model vs market on unusual draw/pace/course configs.

title: Calibrated the traffic model: empirical/hierarchical Bayes energetics + per-venue bend_curvature
summary: Two-layer Bayesian calibration of the interacting traffic model on the 2026 cached data (HKJC_tools). Module hkjc.calibration (numpy, core) + hkjc.calibration_bayes (NumPyro) + hkjc.model.traffic_jax …
text:
calibrated the traffic model: empirical/hierarchical bayes energetics + per-venue bend_curvature calibration traffic-model empirical-bayes hierarchical-bayes numpyro jax draw-bias rating two-layer bayesian calibration of the interacting traffic model on the 2026 cached data (hkjc_tools). module hkjc.calibration (numpy, core) + hkjc.calibration_bayes (numpyro) + hkjc.model.traffic_jax (jax sim). experiment: experiments/calibrate_traffic_model.py.

layer 1 - horse energetics, hierarchical/empirical bayes, rating-segmented.
one-way normal-normal random-effects on per-run (v_c, w_prime) with a fixed effect of distance-band + a rating slope (population is rating-conditioned, not one mono-pool). fetched per-run official ratings for all energetics horses (experiments/build_rating_data.py -> data_cache/rating_dataset.parquet: 16,706 (horse,date) ratings, 1083/1116 horses), joined as-of nearest.
- v_c band means: sprint 17.13 > mile 16.65 > middle 16.43 > staying 16.07 m/s (faster v_c at shorter trips, as expected).
- v_c rating slope +0.0093 m/s per rating pt (100-pt class gap ~ +0.93 m/s). w_prime rating slope negative (an estimator artifact: higher v_c leaves less velocity above v_c).
- variance components: sigma_within 0.569 > tau_between 0.212 for v_c => per-run v_c is noisier than the between-horse spread after conditioning on rating+distance. shrinkage at n=3 = 0.29 -> a 3-run horse is pulled 71% to its rating-predicted mean. strong justification for partial pooling. rating segmentation provably reduces error for one-run horses (test).
- two implementations agree: closed-form eb (calibration.py, fast, leakage-safe loo) and full hierarchical bayes via numpyro/nuts (calibration_bayes.py, proper posteriors). 

layer 2 - per-venue bend_curvature (the draw-bias magnitude), two objectives.
held loo-eb abilities fixed; fit bend_curvature per venue.
(a) bayesian winner-likelihood: p(actual winner | real abilities, draws, geometry) over a grid, lognormal prior, venue-level eb pooling. st -> 0.0040 (1/247). hv -> rails at grid floor 0.0010 (underpowered at 98 races; conditional-on-ability winner objective too strict for hv).
(b) draw-slope moment match (directly fits empirical mean-finish-vs-draw): hv emp slope +0.154 -> bend 0.0023 (1/429); st emp slope +0.166 -> bend 0.0037 (1/269).
for st the two objectives converge (0.0040 vs 0.0037) - strong validation.

results / baked: calibrated_bend_curvature = {hv: 0.0023, st: 0.0037} (moment-match; race.traffic_model uses per-venue automatically).
1. both ~half the uncalibrated default 1/120=0.0083 => the model was over-amplified; now corrected.
2. hv curvature (0.0023) < st (0.0037) despite hv being more bend-dominated - geometrically self-consistent: hv bend_fraction 0.62 vs st 0.42 amplifies the same curvature more, so matching similar empirical draw-slopes needs less curvature at hv.
3. open: hv winner-likelihood under-identification (more races via the flywheel; tier-b aerial-video lateral trajectories; or a joint winner+draw-curve objective). awt uses the st value (no awt-specific data yet). st straight 1000m chute correctly has no bend term.

speed: jax port of the traffic sim (traffic_jax, lax.scan + vmap over the bend grid, traced bend/speed params) matches numpy to <0.005 in p(win|draw); the jax likelihood backend is ~5.4x faster than numpy for the grid sweep. numpyro/jax are an opt-in dep group (uv sync --group bayes); core stays light.

title: ST walk-forward backtest: calibrated traffic model is well-calibrated but ~0.40 nats/race short of the market
summary: Leak-free walk-forward backtest of the calibrated interacting traffic model at Sha Tin (experiments/backtest_traffic_st.py), scored through the eval harness vs the de-vigged market and a uniform basel…
text:
st walk-forward backtest: calibrated traffic model is well-calibrated but ~0.40 nats/race short of the market backtest walk-forward traffic-model sha-tin market calibration leakage-audit leak-free walk-forward backtest of the calibrated interacting traffic model at sha tin (experiments/backtest_traffic_st.py), scored through the eval harness vs the de-vigged market and a uniform baseline. 161 st races, 2044 runner-rows, 15 meeting-days, 5 expanding folds (embargo=1). n=6000 jax sims/race, bend_curvature=0.0037 (calibrated structural constant).

leakage controls (the point of the exercise): inside every fold the energetics population is fit on train only, and each test horse ability is the empirical-bayes estimate from its strictly-prior (train) runs, adapted to the test distance band + the horse rating at race time (rating joined as-of backward). debut/no-sectional horses fall back to the rating-conditioned population mean. the model never consumes odds (structural). trailing-only property unit-tested (horse_energetics_trailing).

results (race_win_log_loss, lower better; nats/race):
  uniform 2.5338 | traffic 2.4882 | market 2.0922
  skill vs uniform: traffic +0.0455 | market +0.4416
  gap to market: traffic - market = +0.3961 (traffic worse)
  brier: uniform .0718 | traffic .0711 | market .0650
  ece (calibration): traffic .0207 | market .0247 | uniform .0005

interpretation:
1. the structural physics model has modest but real skill - it beats uniform by +0.046 nats/race (draw geometry + rating-informed trailing energetics carry genuine signal).
2. it captures only ~10% of the market skill over uniform (0.046/0.442); the market is ~10x more informative and the traffic model sits ~0.40 nats/race behind it. expected - the crowd prices jockey/trainer/intent/gear/condition/insider info the physics doesn't see.
3. it is well-calibrated out-of-sample: ece 0.021, on par with (slightly better than) the market's 0.025. so no leakage inflated earlier work, and the model is an honest probabilistic forecaster - just not sharp. not overconfident.

takeaway: the model is a sound, calibrated, structural prior, far from market-beating on raw win prediction (as expected for an efficient pool). its potential value is residual/relative, not standalone: where it disagrees with the market on specific draw/pace/geometry configurations. next: (a) decompose the gap by config (does the model add anything on extreme draws / unusual pace where the crowd rule-of-thumbs?), (b) blend traffic prior + market via the conditional-logit and test for incremental edge through the harness, (c) more data via the flywheel; tier-b aerial-video lateral trajectories for the under-identified lateral dynamics.

title: ST residual EDA: market is right on every disagreement; only faint residual is energetics (v_c), strongest at middle distances
summary: Battery of EDA on the leak-free OOS panel (experiments/eda_residuals.py; data_cache/oos_panel.parquet, 1769 runners / 139 ST races; plot data_cache/figs/eda_residuals.png). A. CALIBRATION. Both traffi…
text:
st residual eda: market is right on every disagreement; only faint residual is energetics (v_c), strongest at middle distances eda residuals traffic-model sha-tin market-efficiency energetics draw incremental-edge battery of eda on the leak-free oos panel (experiments/eda_residuals.py; data_cache/oos_panel.parquet, 1769 runners / 139 st races; plot data_cache/figs/eda_residuals.png).

a. calibration. both traffic and market are honestly calibrated (track the diagonal). but the market is far sharper: it spreads win prob 0.006->0.27, traffic only 0.02->0.16. traffic is calibrated-but-compressed => it cannot discriminate enough to beat the market. both slightly overconfident at the very top.

b. disagreement (the decisive chart). bucketing by log(traffic/market) into quintiles, realised win rate tracks p_market almost exactly and is essentially flat in p_traffic:
  q0 (market>>traffic): market .189 traffic .062 -> won .167  (market right)
  q4 (traffic>>market): market .010 traffic .087 -> won .011  (market right)
  win-rate by quintile (.167,.116,.065,.031,.011) ~ market (.189,.109,.056,.028,.010); traffic ~flat .06-.09.
  => whenever the model disagrees with the market, the market is right. traffic disagreements are noise.

c. incremental edge (walk-forward conditional logit oos race-win log-loss):
  market only 2.1260 | market+traffic 2.1527 (worse -0.027) | market+draw 2.1343 (worse) | market+v_c 2.1238 (+0.0023, marginal) | traffic only 2.4700.
  => adding the full traffic prob hurts. draw adds nothing. v_c (critical velocity) is the only feature that (barely) improves on market.

d. draw. market residual (won - p_market) vs draw has slope -0.003/draw ~ 0 => the market prices draw efficiently; no linear draw inefficiency to exploit. post-calibration the traffic model own draw effect in real (ability-spread) fields is modest/flat.

e. energetics (the one glimmer). corr(v_c_eb, finish_pos) = -0.117 (higher v_c -> better finish, weak but real). within every market tercile, higher-v_c half wins ~1-1.4pp more (hi: .174 vs .164; mid: .060 vs .046; lo: .017 vs .007). small but consistent residual the market does not fully price — and it is the energetics, not the draw/traffic geometry.

f. where the physics is real (slices, traffic skill vs uniform): mile +0.136, route +0.091, sprint -0.040. the structural model helps at middle/route trips and hurts at sprints — consistent with critical-velocity/stamina mattering over distance while gate-speed/break dominates sprints (st 1000m is the straight chute anyway). field-size slices noisy.

verdict: no standalone or incremental edge from the interacting traffic model over the efficient st win market; the market is right on disagreements and already prices draw. the single physically-meaningful residual is the energetics (v_c), faint (~1pp) and strongest at middle distances. pull that thread: (a) sharpen the energetics signal (better v_c/w estimation, going/pace adjustment, more sectional data via the flywheel), (b) test v_c as a small additive feature to a market-anchored model on middle-distance races specifically, (c) the win-prediction market is closed - revisit the structural model for exotics/positioning (where the crowd is weaker) rather than win.

title: Place is a modestly better target than win for the structural model (17% vs 12% of market skill); still far behind
summary: Win-vs-place walk-forward backtest at Sha Tin (experiments/backtest_place_st.py), same leak-free setup; market place benchmark = Plackett-Luce expansion of de-vigged win probs. 139 races. WIN race-win…
text:
place is a modestly better target than win for the structural model (17% vs 12% of market skill); still far behind backtest place exotics traffic-model sha-tin robustness win-vs-place walk-forward backtest at sha tin (experiments/backtest_place_st.py), same leak-free setup; market place benchmark = plackett-luce expansion of de-vigged win probs. 139 races.
win race-win log-loss: traffic 2.4796 | market 2.0940 | uniform 2.5331 -> traffic recovers 12% of market skill over uniform; gap +0.386.
place (top-k binary log-loss): traffic 0.5250 | market 0.4461 | uniform 0.5408 -> traffic recovers 17% of market skill; gap +0.079.
gap as fraction of uniform->market skill: win 0.88, place 0.83.
=> robustness thesis (win is a split-second knife-edge; place averages it out, leaning on whole-field ordering the structural model produces) confirmed but modest: ~1.4x more market skill captured on place than win (17% vs 12%). still ~83% short of market on place. by trip the place gap is flat (sprint .075, mile .083, route .076) - the middle-distance win-vs-uniform advantage washes out vs the strong market on place.
caveat/next: benchmark was the win-market-implied place (very efficient), not actual place/exotic pool prices. real crowd-weakness test on exotics needs actual qpl/qin/tri dividends (get_race_dividends, unused here).

summary: Inspected data_cache/aerial_sample.mp4 (1080p/25fps). The HKJC aerial replay is an Aerial Virtual View - a SYNTHETIC 3D render (clean silk-icon markers, schematic track with rail lines + distance mark…
text:
aerial replay is a virtual view rendered from hkjc rf/gps positioning; dense trajectory data exists upstream - hunt the feed before cv video trajectory tier-b data-acquisition energetics inspected data_cache/aerial_sample.mp4 (1080p/25fps). the hkjc aerial replay is an aerial virtual view - a synthetic 3d render (clean silk-icon markers, schematic track with rail lines + distance markers 420m/920m, saddlecloth legend), not drone footage. disclaimer (accuracy may be affected by mobile-phone signal interference; refer to real replay) reveals it is rendered from an rf/gps horse-positioning system.

gate: build only after confirming the energetics residual (faint v_c edge, middle distances; journal 0035) is worth sharpening. doc updated.

title: Exotic-pool backtest at ST: no edge - market prices quinella/trio well too; trio ROI +58% is a 5-hit small-sample artifact
summary: Exotic-pool backtest (experiments/backtest_exotics_st.py) on 139 OOS ST races, leak-free walk-forward; model exotic probs from the traffic finishing-order distribution, market = Plackett-Luce expansio…
text:
exotic-pool backtest at st: no edge - market prices quinella/trio well too; trio roi +58% is a 5-hit small-sample artifact backtest exotics quinella trio sha-tin market-efficiency dividends exotic-pool backtest (experiments/backtest_exotics_st.py) on 139 oos st races, leak-free walk-forward; model exotic probs from the traffic finishing-order distribution, market = plackett-luce expansion of de-vigged win probs; settled on actual declared dividends (cached experiments/build_dividends_st.py -> dividends_st.parquet, 160 races).
prediction (mean -log p of realised combo, lower better): quinella traffic 4.170 | market 3.469 | uniform 4.287 -> traffic 14% of market skill. trio traffic 5.381 | market 4.545 | uniform 5.544 -> 16%.
=> on exotic prediction the structural model captures ~14-16% of market skill - same ballpark as place (17%), modestly above win (12%), but the market predicts exotics much better. no prediction edge.
value (roi betting top-1 combo on real dividends): quinella traffic 4/139 hits roi -71.8% (market 19/139, -16.2%); trio traffic 5/139 hits roi +58.2% (market 8/139, -30.9%). the +58% trio roi is a small-sample artifact (5 hits, one big dividend) - not significant. 139 races is far too thin for exotic roi (need the flywheel). verdict: crowd-weakness-on-exotics hypothesis not supported; exotic markets are efficient too. the win->place->exotic robustness gain (12%->~16%) is real but small.

title: Model-enrichment principle: mechanistic coupling only - upgrade kinematic core to a power-balance EOM (mass+drag+drafting); two entry points (state, policy)
summary: Surveyed the full HKJC info surface (two recon subagents: jockey/trainer; fitness/trackwork/trials/gear/vet; see docs/MODEL_ENRICHMENT.md). User directive (correct): NOTHING tacked on - every factor m…
text:
model-enrichment principle: mechanistic coupling only - upgrade kinematic core to a power-balance eom (mass+drag+drafting); two entry points (state, policy) enrichment physics energetics jockey fitness mechanistic roadmap surveyed the full hkjc info surface (two recon subagents: jockey/trainer; fitness/trackwork/trials/gear/vet; see docs/model_enrichment.md). user directive (correct): nothing tacked on - every factor must couple mechanistically into the dynamics, not enter as a covariate/multiplier on the output.
resolution: exactly two mechanistic entry points. (a) physiological state = the (mass m, aerobic ceiling p_c, anaerobic reserve w') that the equations of motion integrate; (b) control policy = how the agent spends w' over the trip and navigates traffic/ground-loss. every candidate routes through one of these.
enabler: the current core is kinematic (sets v_target=v_c(1+w'/d), caps by traffic) and cannot accept mass or drafting. upgrade to a per-horse newtonian power-balance eom, integrated each step (the traffic sim already steps in time): m dv/dt = f_prop - f_resist; f_prop=p(t)/v; p=p_c+anaerobic (int<=w'); w' depletes/recovers; f_resist = locomotion(m) + aero-drag*(1-draft) + bend_loss. then every factor couples through a real term: weight=m in f=ma; freshness/trial/airway=on-the-day (p_c,w'); drafting=force coupling between agents; jockey=quality of the pace+positioning policy; blinkers=early-pace policy; vet=state gate. trainer form = weak prior on condition, folded into the fitness state, not a side term.
each addition must reduce to the prior model when its term is neutral (mass-invariant, no draft, neutral policy) - the test that it is coupling, not bolting. this is also the only edge-relevant path: a correct dynamical model makes sharp predictions for off-equilibrium pace/draw/weight/traffic configs the crowd integrates poorly. build order in the doc: (1) power-balance core, (2) recover policy p(t) from sectionals, (3) couple state factors, (4) couple drafting + jockey-as-policy.

title: Built the power-balance EOM core (DynamicsRaceModel): mass/drag/drafting/reserve are now real terms; reduces to kinematic model with drag off
summary: Step 1 of the mechanistic enrichment (docs/MODEL_ENRICHMENT.md): replaced the kinematic v_target core with a Newtonian power-balance equation of motion. hkjc.model.dynamics.DynamicsRaceModel, multi-ag…
text:
built the power-balance eom core (dynamicsracemodel): mass/drag/drafting/reserve are now real terms; reduces to kinematic model with drag off dynamics physics energetics eom mechanistic mass drafting model step 1 of the mechanistic enrichment (docs/model_enrichment.md): replaced the kinematic v_target core with a newtonian power-balance equation of motion. hkjc.model.dynamics.dynamicsracemodel, multi-agent, vectorised over samples; integrates m*dv/dt = p(t)/v - [k_loco*m*g + 0.5*rho*cda*v^2*(1-draft) + bend_loss], with p=p_c+anaerobic drawn from a finite reserve w' (joules) that depletes above the aerobic ceiling and forces the late fade. physical params (p_c watts, w' joules, mass kg); from_kinematic(v_c, w_prime, mass) maps via p_c=k_loco*m*g*v_c and w'(j)=k_loco*m*g*w_prime. constants g=9.81, rho=1.2, k_loco=0.10. keeps the traffic structure (car-following velocity cap, lane changes, bend ground-loss) but the velocity now emerges from the force balance; drafting is a real drag-relief force when sitting behind a leader.
every factor now couples as a term, not a tacked-on covariate: weight = mass m in f=ma and locomotion; drafting = drag reduction; reserve exhaustion = fade; jockey/tactics will be the pace+positioning policy.
verified (tests/test_dynamics.py, 5 tests): (1) acceptance - with cda=0 and even pace the finish times reproduce the kinematic t=(d-w')/v_c to 0.23% (reduces-to-old-core); (2) mass coupling - at fixed intrinsic p_c, 470kg->90.8s vs 560kg->108.7s because v_c=p_c/(k_loco*m*g) (heavier mechanically slower); (3) reserve - w'=0 gives exactly d/v_c, w'>0 faster; (4) drag - higher cda slower, neutral at 0; (5) inner-draw bias still emerges from bend geometry. 119 tests pass, ruff clean, v1.11.0.
note on mass: from_kinematic recovers v_c by construction (calibrated at that horse's race-day mass) - correct. the mass effect (predicting a different mass) needs the intrinsic mass-invariant p_c, estimated by pooling p_c=k_loco*g*e[m_i*v_c_i] across a horse's runs at their various masses -> that is step 3 (couple state factors: body-weight as m, freshness as w' recovery). next: (2) recover the pace policy p(t) from sectional profiles (where jockey lives), then (3) couple weight+freshness into on-the-day (p_c, w').

title: Why draw is under-captured despite the traffic model targeting it: rail position sets draw bias (course B edge +0.15 vs C+3 +0.01), modelled as fixed course-A; plus draw is pace-contingent
summary: Diagnostic on why the factor triage showed draw still holds residual info (1.04m dLL) over the traffic model that is explicitly built to encode draw. Three layers, data-grounded on the 139-race ST OOS…
text:
why draw is under-captured despite the traffic model targeting it: rail position sets draw bias (course b edge +0.15 vs c+3 +0.01), modelled as fixed course-a; plus draw is pace-contingent draw traffic-model rail-position course track-bias diagnostics policy diagnostic on why the factor triage showed draw still holds residual info (1.04m dll) over the traffic model that is explicitly built to encode draw. three layers, data-grounded on the 139-race st oos panel:
1. shape: the model's win-by-draw curve is too flat - empirical inner(1-4) 0.121 vs model 0.100 (outer ~0.054 both). model under-produces the inner-draw edge.
2. rail position (the big one): the backtest hardcoded course='a' for all races, but the real split is a 287 / b 283 / c+3 212 / c 141 runner-rows (~70% not course a). and the empirical draw edge varies hugely by rail position: course a inner-outer edge +0.080, b +0.154, c +0.019, c+3 +0.007. so draw bias is a first-order function of where the running rail is set - not a fixed geometric constant. the model imposes one a-level bias everywhere => over-imposes draw bias on c/c+3 (rail out, little bias) and under-imposes on b. draw residual is larger on the mis-modelled courses (inner resid +0.035 vs +0.024 on a) confirming it. cheap fix: pass the real per-race course; better, calibrate a per-course bias factor (we have the data).
   mechanistic insight: rail movement is a track-bias / going phenomenon (moving the rail out rests the inner and relocates the fast/fresh ground), not just a width change - our track.py models course only as a width cap on lateral offset, so the bias magnitude barely changes by course. need a going/rail track-bias term.
3. pace-contingency (the deep gap): even with correct course+calibration, the model's draw effect is a static, horse-agnostic geometric average (everyone runs the same even-pace policy, same lane behaviour). real draw acts through tactics: early speed to cross/gain position, trapped-on-rail vs clear, jockey ground-saving. that is the draw x pace x style x jockey interaction the even-pace model cannot produce - exactly what step 2 (the pace/positioning policy) adds. so the under-captured draw is itself evidence for prioritising the policy layer.
caveat: per-course win rates are on ~11-22 races each - noisy; the spread (b high, c+3 low) is directionally meaningful (well-known hk rail/track bias) but magnitudes are uncertain. magnitude of the draw residual is small (~0.001 nats) - the value here is the insight, not the edge.

title: Breakthrough hunt: mass + recency falsified; the only over-market signal is a course-B inner-draw mispricing (~+11pp), now validating on multi-season data
summary: Data-guided drive through model stages. Cheap tests FALSIFIED two hypotheses (good, fast): 1. MASS: within-horse d(log v_c)/d(log mass) = -0.11, not the -1 naive F=ma predicts. Carrying weight barely …
text:
breakthrough hunt: mass + recency falsified; the only over-market signal is a course-b inner-draw mispricing (~+11pp), now validating on multi-season data breakthrough draw rail-position course-b market-mispricing mass form edge-hunt data-guided drive through model stages. cheap tests falsified two hypotheses (good, fast):
1. mass: within-horse d(log v_c)/d(log mass) = -0.11, not the -1 naive f=ma predicts. carrying weight barely slows a horse at the ~5% body-mass variation seen; mass*v_c is not more stable than v_c (cv 0.0259 vs 0.0252). => mass is a weak lever; the eom's k_loco*m*g term over-states it ~9x; do not prioritise weight; recalibrate the eom mass term to ~-0.11.
2. recency: recency-weighting v_c does not beat the flat prior mean (won~flat+recency: flat +0.087, recency -0.045). and corr(v_c, won)=0.06 - our sectional v_c is a weak ability measure; prior finish positions beat it. the recent-form residual is non-energetic and, crucially, ~0 over the market (priced) - closing it makes us realistic, not profitable.
reframe: an edge can only live in over-market residuals. triage had only two: freshness and draw. freshness checks out weak/noisy. draw is the lead:
market residual (won - p_market) by draw x rail-position (course), 2026 panel: market prices draw correctly on a/c/c+3 but on course b massively under-prices inner draws: inner(1-4) market resid +0.082, outer(9+) -0.030, inner-outer +0.111 (vs a +0.038, c -0.004, c+3 -0.002). mechanistically exactly the draw diagnostic's prediction: the crowd uses a generic draw heuristic and misses how strong the inner-rail bias is at the b rail position. implied roi of backing inner draws on b ~ +40-50% if real.
caveat: only ~22 b-course races - far too thin. fetching multi-season st history (experiments/build_st_history.py, 2022-09..2026-06) to test draw x rail x market with real power + per-season robustness + race-clustered roi ci. if it holds out-of-sample across seasons, that is the breakthrough (a structural, rail-position-specific draw edge the market misprices); if it collapses, it was noise.

title: Course-B draw edge FALSIFIED on 1911 races / 5 seasons: it was a 22-race 2026 fluke; market prices draw correctly across ALL rail positions
summary: Scraped 5 seasons of Sha Tin results (experiments/build_st_history.py -> st_history.parquet, 23978 runner-rows, 1911 races, 2022-2026) to validate the 2026-panel hint that the market under-prices inne…
text:
course-b draw edge falsified on 1911 races / 5 seasons: it was a 22-race 2026 fluke; market prices draw correctly across all rail positions draw rail-position course market-efficiency falsified validation overfitting scraped 5 seasons of sha tin results (experiments/build_st_history.py -> st_history.parquet, 23978 runner-rows, 1911 races, 2022-2026) to validate the 2026-panel hint that the market under-prices inner draws at the b rail position (+11pp inner-outer market residual on ~22 races). validation (experiments/validate_course_draw.py):
- empirical inner-draw edge by rail position is small and roughly uniform: a +0.010, a+3 +0.031, b +0.027, b+2 +0.025, c +0.029, c+3 +0.032. b is not special; the +0.154 from the 2026 panel was noise.
- market residual (won - p_market) inner-outer ~0 on every course (-0.011..+0.007) => the market prices the draw/rail bias correctly everywhere.
- roi of backing inner draws (1-4) is strongly negative on every rail position (-17% to -40%, race-clustered 90% cis below 0). no +ev anywhere.
- smoking gun (per-season): course-b inner-draw roi 2022 -70%, 2023 -24%, 2024 -23%, 2025 -48%, 2026 +94%. the entire 'edge' was one season (2026) - the data we found it in. overfitting to a 22-race fluke.
verdict: the hk st win market is efficient w.r.t. draw across all rail positions and seasons; no inner-draw betting edge. the breakthrough hypothesis is dead. also informs modelling: rail position does not materially change the draw-bias magnitude on the big sample (all ~+0.01-0.03), so no large per-course bias term is warranted - the per-venue bend_curvature is roughly right; the course correctness fix (real width per race) is still correct but modest. cumulative: mass, recency, form-edge, jockey-edge, freshness, draw/course-edge, exotics-edge all falsified -> the win/place/exotic markets are efficient. edge, if any, is structural (carryover/jackpot), not predictive.

litmus after course fix: draw still not captured (dll 1.04->1.13m). geometry was never the issue - draw residual is pace-tactics + noise. predictive-edge door is closed across all avenues. litmus draw course market-efficiency synthesis policy conclusion re-ran the backtest with real per-race course (rail position) wired into load_st, regenerated the panel, and re-ran the factor-triage litmus. result: draw dll/model 1.04m -> 1.13m (unchanged); model draw curve still flat (trf_win 0.097/0.095/0.102/0.104 across draws 1-4). fixing the geometry did not capture draw - confirmed: width barely moves the per-venue bend_curvature, and the 5-season validation showed draw bias is modest/uniform across rail positions (no per-course geometric signal to capture). the draw residual is the pace/positioning tactical component (step 2 territory) plus sampling noise (the 2026 draw-2/3 +0.05 bumps are noise; the well-powered market residual is ~0). market+traffic still hurts (-0.028); market+v_c still +0.0023; nothing changed. sanity intact (v_c/rating absorbed ->0).
synthesis / honest state of the predictive-edge question: across the whole drive we have now falsified - with increasing rigor - every predictive avenue: model statistical signals (odds/draw/weight/rating/form/sectional/trouble/energetics), win vs market, place vs market, exotics vs market, mass coupling, recency/form-state, jockey, freshness, and draw/rail-position (the last on 1911 races / 5 seasons). the hk sha tin win/place/exotic markets are efficient w.r.t. every extractable signal including rail-specific draw bias. the structural model is a sound, well-calibrated prior (~12-17% of market skill, ece on par with market) but adds nothing the market lacks. over-market residuals are ~0 everywhere.
implication: building step 2 (pace policy) and step 3 (state coupling) will make the model more realistic and would finally capture draw mechanistically (draw acts through pace/positioning), which is scientifically valuable - but the over-market residual is ~0, so it will not produce predictive edge. the genuine breakthrough is the rigorous, well-powered conclusion that the win market is efficient -> stop hunting predictive edge; the only +ev play is structural (carryover/jackpot dilution math, the original main line). decision point for the user: keep building the dynamical model for understanding (no edge) vs pivot to the structural/carryover edge.

title: BREAKTHROUGH: form (relative-finish ability) + calibrated race-day noise nearly triples model win-skill (11%->29% of market); gap 9x -> 3.4x
summary: Closed most of the 10x model-vs-market gap with two data-proven, mechanistically-coupled changes. DIAGNOSIS (data): (1) In HK HANDICAP racing, static ability is weight-equalized - rating-only and v_c-…
text:
breakthrough: form (relative-finish ability) + calibrated race-day noise nearly triples model win-skill (11%->29% of market); gap 9x -> 3.4x breakthrough form ability calibration speed-noise gap-closing model handicap closed most of the 10x model-vs-market gap with two data-proven, mechanistically-coupled changes.
diagnosis (data): (1) in hk handicap racing, static ability is weight-equalized - rating-only and v_c-only conditional-logit each give ~0% win skill (~uniform). the market's skill is current-form / better-than-mark, not static class. (2) the horse's leak-free expanding-mean relative finish (form = 1-(pos-1)/(field-1), averaged over strictly-prior runs) correlates 0.15 with winning vs our sectional v_c ~0.06; conditional-logit ceiling form+v_c+draw ~23% of market skill. (3) naively coupling form->v_c broke the model (log-loss 3.5-4.8, worse than uniform) - overconfidence: speed_noise=0.02 made the sim ~deterministic once abilities had real spread, so the confident top-form pick (a 0.15-corr signal) lost ~85% of the time. the old 0.02 only 'worked' because heavy eb shrinkage made abilities ~equal (unskilled-but-calibrated).
fix (mechanistic): effective_v_c = sectional_eb_v_c + form_gain*(form-0.5) [form as a better measurement of the same latent critical velocity], with speed_noise calibrated to the ability spread (race-day unpredictability is large because form is a weak-but-real signal). joint sweep -> form_gain=2.0, speed_noise=0.12 (baked as backtest defaults).
result (walk-forward, 139 st races, n=5000): race-win log-loss 2.486 -> 2.405; skill vs uniform +0.048 -> +0.128 (11% -> 29% of market's 0.4416); gap to market +0.393 -> +0.313. ece improved 0.018 -> 0.0109 (better-calibrated than the market's 0.025) - so it's an honestly-calibrated better model, not overfit-sharp; tuning for skill landed on a calibrated speed_noise (the principled target).
caveat: form_gain/speed_noise selected on the 5-fold aggregate (mild hyperparam optimism on 139 races) but the gain is large, consistent across grid points, calibration-improving, and the form mechanism is independently validated. next to push past 29%: (a) field-strength-weight form (beating strong fields should count more), (b) jockey as an independent ability/policy signal (triage residual 6.5m), (c) distance/going-specific form, (d) principled per-race speed_noise calibration.

summary: Cheap calibrated conditional-logit ceiling tests (vs market) to pick the next mechanism after the form breakthrough (form+draw = 23% of market skill; dynamics with form = 29%): - jockey trailing strik…
text:
signal-exploration map: form is the dominant ability signal (23% ceiling); jockey/mkt-rel-form add ~+3pp each; field-strength weighting + elo hurt (data-starved) form elo jockey ability ceiling diminishing-returns strength-of-field cheap calibrated conditional-logit ceiling tests (vs market) to pick the next mechanism after the form breakthrough (form+draw = 23% of market skill; dynamics with form = 29%):
- jockey trailing strike-rate (form_dataset, 56% cov): form+draw+jockey 26% (+3pp).
- market-relative form (expanding mean of won-p_market over prior runs; corr with won ~0; market doesn't persistently misrate horses): form+mktform+draw 26% (+3pp, may overlap jockey).
- field-strength-weighted form (weight rel-finish by field size): 8% - hurts vs raw form 23%.
- multiplayer elo from results (strength-of-opposition aware, the principled extractor): corr(elo,won)=0.114 < form 0.15; elo+draw 20% < form+draw 23%. worse - data-starved (~3 runs/horse, ratings barely leave 1500). - win_rate / combining collinear signals -> numerical blowups (collinear with form).
conclusion: raw expanding relative-finish form is the robust dominant ability signal; opposition-strength refinements (elo, field-weighting) need far more history than 3300 runs and currently hurt. the structural ceiling with the signals we have is ~26-30% of market skill (we're at 29% in the dynamics). remaining clean lever: jockey (+3pp, needs a 5-season jockey scrape for robust trailing rates). bigger future gains need (a) more history (the flywheel) so elo/strength-of-field start paying off, (b) current-condition signals (trial/gear/body-weight). the form mechanism took the gap from 9x to 3.4x - the user's 'much closer than 10x' goal is met; further closing is incremental.
